recommendation: Choose Option 3, then the Class A opening, with Option 2's pre-SATISFIED-GRADE sequencing. If v3 remains the final subject, obtain fresh application-grade dual review of v3; if a v4 successor is authored, review v4 rather than v3. Before SATISFIED-GRADE, author DR-133 NT-6 fixtures, establish the byte-recorded NT-4/NT-7 fixture standing at G20 and author them if still unauthored, and separately record or remove the candidate's proposed file-01 preview-role delta. A shared three-row Gate-2 entry is lawful only with a separate DR-133 finding.
rationale: Claude correctly rejects promotion of the existing candidate-grade verdicts: the Claude verdict leaves application grade to the coordinator, the Codex verdict does not, and D-001 requires an application-grade independent review. The current G21 join also names DR-133 NT-6 among unauthored classes, while the current G20 join does not name NT-4 or NT-7, so the strict D-056 path should resolve those bytes before SATISFIED-GRADE. The programme is incomplete without one further candidate-review finding: Claude's existing v3 verdict says the file-01 preview-role delta is proposed but not adopted and requires a separate reviewed act. D-136 did not perform that act. Also, D-147's row-level Gates 2 and 3 finding is not automatically superseded by later gate-row fixture measurements; the shared ruling must reconcile that scope rather than assume a contradiction. With those amendments, the proposed fresh review, per-row opening, fixture work, and later per-row SATISFIED-GRADE cycle are sound under D-056.

refutations.claim: The live DR-133 row records provider-only-output-contract.v3 only as a non-applied candidate and leaves the row OPEN.
refutations.evidence: File 08 DR-133 names digest ef2a7416700cc8197486c6e29450673c60e3b94512be3ad278d1995f7d281309 and says CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, binds NOTHING, and Not SATISFIED; D-136 says Class A is not opened.

refutations.claim: The existing verdict pair is candidate-grade rather than application-grade.
refutations.evidence: The Claude acceptanceGrade says 'design-contract candidate' and its coordinatorSummary says 'candidate only'; the Codex authority note says it is review evidence on the candidate bytes only. Neither verdict grants application-grade acceptance.

refutations.claim: Only the Claude verdict says application grade is a coordinator determination.
refutations.evidence: Claude whatThisAcceptanceDoesNotDo states that whether the recording is application-grade is a coordinator determination. The Codex verdict contains no equivalent delegation and instead denies application, seal, owner grant, and row disposition.

refutations.claim: A fresh application-grade review removes the Gate-1 candidate-only objection.
refutations.evidence: D-001 requires the independent review itself to grant application-grade acceptance with no express reservation. A new neutral verdict pair on the final subject bytes supplies evidence the existing reviews expressly withhold.

refutations.claim: Current bytes leave DR-133 NT-6 unauthored at G21 and do not state NT-4/NT-7 fixture standing in the G20 join.
refutations.evidence: g21-leftover-join.v13 lists DR-133 NT-6 among remaining unauthored classes and says it does not author NT-6. g20-leftover-join.v6 contains neither DR-133 nor NT-4 nor NT-7; no g20 fixture-corpus artifact is present, while the G20 occupancy routes NT-4/NT-7 there.

refutations.claim: D-292 automatically overturns D-147's finding that DR-133 Gates 2 and 3 hold.
refutations.evidence: D-147 is a row-level finding after naming all seven NT classes. D-292 records a G21 gate remasurement, preserves separate fixture-authoring work, says it does not SATISFY DR-133, and contains no DR-133 Gate-2 supersession. The two scopes create a review risk but not an express overturn.

refutations.claim: Option 4 has no byte-recorded 'what must change' beyond the three advisories.
refutations.evidence: The existing Claude verdict says adoption of the file-01 preview-role delta is a separate reviewed act. Current joins also expose NT-6 authoring and unresolved NT-4/NT-7 fixture standing. Those are byte-recorded issues independent of the advisories.

refutations.claim: Deferring DR-133 would conflict with the recorded disposition.
refutations.evidence: D-134 places DR-133 in the SATISFIED-requiring set, while D-132 authorizes the provider-only contract work. No adopted entry supplies a DR-133 deferral route.

refutations.claim: The proposed programme can ignore the file-01 preview-role delta.
refutations.evidence: provider-only-output-contract.v3 describes a preview-role delta, and the Claude review explicitly says the verdict does not adopt it and that recording it is a separate reviewed act. D-136 records the candidate but does not record that delta as applied law.

refutations.claim: D-000 requires a separate Gate-2 ruling heading for each of DR-131, DR-133, and DR-117.
refutations.evidence: D-000 has no one-row-per-entry rule and permits a fully documented shared decision. The later D-056 Gate-4 requirement is different: it demands a dedicated SATISFIED-GRADE review of each row.

amendments: Make the fresh application-grade reviews target whichever artifact version the opening entry actually cites.
Add a separate reviewed disposition of the file-01 preview-role delta, or remove reliance on that delta, before the DR-133 SATISFIED-GRADE cycle.
Treat NT-6 authoring as established work; byte-resolve NT-4/NT-7 at G20 before deciding what authoring is required there.
In the shared Gate-2 entry, reconcile D-147 with the current gate joins instead of declaring that the later gate measurement silently superseded the row finding.
